title: Understanding Cross-Domain Adaptation in Low-Resource Topic Modeling
subcategory: domain adaptation for low-resource topic modelling
task: Topic modelling of small target corpora with help from a large source corpus
problem: Few target documents give unstable topics; naive transfer floods the target with irrelevant source topics.
architecture: Finite-sample generalisation bound (source and target reconstruction, latent discrepancy, decoder consistency, KL regularisation). DALTA: shared VAE encoder for domain-invariant features, separate source/target decoders, adversarial domain discriminator to align latent distributions, KL regulariser.

datasets.name: 20 Newsgroups
datasets.details: Science and Religion subsets as targets, 1,000 documents each

key_results: Highest CV in every target and k (e.g. Norethindrone k = 10: 0.582 vs FASTopic 0.517).
TD is not always best (e.g. Norethindrone k = 20: 0.800 vs FASTopic 0.948).
strengths: Theory-guided design for low-resource topic modelling.
Evaluates coherence, diversity, classification and clustering.

limitations.text: No practical method to choose the best source domain; effect of different sources not studied; transfer can hurt when topic structures differ.
